nodes.label: Barème des séries de Torī (0/2/4/7/10)
nodes.rationale: A player may score several series of distinct colors, but a given physical Torī can never belong to two series — which is what makes the grouping a combinatorial optimisation. Worked example in the rulebook: 8 Torī → 12 PV (5 distinct + 2 distinct + 1).

nodes.label: Greedy Torī series grouping
nodes.rationale: 'Peel one of every color still available, repeat' always finds the maximum-scoring grouping and reproduces the rulebook's own worked example (8 Torī → 12 VP), so the user enters raw counts and never has to plan the grouping.

nodes.label: Oracle Kotlin legacy/1ksabord-kotlin
nodes.rationale: Gardé temporairement comme oracle : ses 107 tests tournent en CI. Il disparaîtra avec les dépôts satellites ; les fixtures golden restent.

nodes.label: ResultatScore
nodes.rationale: Non sérialisé directement : il n'existe qu'en mémoire, c'est CoupCalculateur qui est persisté.

nodes.label: Invariants de Partie
nodes.rationale: Un joueur ne joue pas deux tours consécutifs ; dépasser 6000 déclenche le dernier tour ; seul le dernier coup est annulable ; la victoire par pirate magique est immédiate.

nodes.label: assertRoundsSumToRanking (invariant de sortie)
nodes.rationale: Les manches d'un joueur doivent sommer à son score de classement, sans quoi l'import de Scoreo rejetterait la partie.

nodes.label: LancerDes (objet valeur immuable)
nodes.rationale: Le Kotlin en faisait des méthodes d'instance ; en TypeScript ce sont des fonctions libres sur une donnée immuable.

nodes.label: EvenementCoup (union discriminée)
nodes.rationale: Là où le Kotlin avait une sealed class, le TypeScript a une union discriminée sur `type` et la méthode abstraite devient la fonction libre contributionPour().

nodes.label: Test différentiel golden (preuve du portage)
nodes.rationale: Le domaine est une transposition ligne à ligne du Kotlin, vérifiée et non relue : tests/golden/ rejoue un corpus de parties des deux côtés et compare l'enveloppe v1.1 octet pour octet. Aucun des deux ne peut dériver sans que l'autre passe au rouge.

nodes.label: Ids de dés en anglais ('skulls', 'diamonds', …)
nodes.rationale: Hérités du HTML de l'app Kotlin et conservés par le portage : ce sont eux que le corpus golden sérialise, donc les renommer casserait la comparaison octet pour octet.

nodes.label: Repli à zéro (Math.max(0, acc + contribution))
nodes.rationale: Porté par totalJoueurParNom (privée) : sans ce plancher à zéro appliqué à chaque événement, les manches ne somment plus au classement et l'import de Scoreo rejette la partie.

nodes.label: Une instance par état, pas un singleton
nodes.norm_label: une instance par etat, pas un singleton
nodes.rationale: L'app Kotlin partageait un `val partie` global. L'agrégat est mutable : le garder dans l'état du réducteur ferait dépendre sa sortie de qui d'autre en détient une référence. L'écran garde donc le journal et rejoue l'agrégat via partieDeLEtat(state).

nodes.label: Event sourcing (journal d'EvenementCoup)
nodes.rationale: Chaque action de jeu est un EvenementCoup stocké dans l'historique ; les totaux se dérivent du journal au lieu d'être stockés à côté.

nodes.label: Immutabilité (champs readonly)
nodes.rationale: LancerDes et ResultatScore n'ont que des champs readonly : une modification produit une copie.

nodes.label: Pureté du calcul de score
nodes.rationale: calculerScore() n'a aucun effet de bord ni état global.

nodes.label: Sérialisation zod avec .default() par champ
nodes.rationale: Chaque objet métier a son schéma *Schema avec un .default() par champ ajouté : c'est ce qui permet à un brouillon écrit par une version antérieure de se relire.

nodes.label: Les trois garde-fous du brouillon
nodes.rationale: 1) version en z.literal, pas un nombre : un brouillon d'une autre version échoue à la validation et l'écran repart propre au lieu de ressusciter une demi-forme ancienne. 2) La même table : un brouillon dont les joueurs ne sont pas ceux passés par l'hôte est ignoré, sinon une partie abandonnée réapparaîtrait au milieu d'une autre. 3) Rouvrir gagne : quand editing est présent, c'est sa charge qui est lue.

nodes.label: L'agrégat Partie est délibérément absent de l'état
nodes.norm_label: l'agregat partie est deliberement absent de l'etat
nodes.rationale: L'agrégat est mutable : en garder un dans l'état ferait dépendre la sortie du réducteur de qui d'autre en détient une référence. C'est la traduction du `val partie` global du Kotlin : ce que le singleton portait, le journal le porte, sans le partager.

nodes.label: Les actions du réducteur
nodes.rationale: quickSkullIsland frappe les adversaires, pas le joueur courant ; undoLast délègue à Partie.annulerDernier() qui rejoue tout l'historique — du domaine déjà porté et vérifié.

nodes.label: Les dérivations (rien n'est stocké)
nodes.rationale: partieDeLEtat, joueurActuel, estFinie, versBrouillon, etatInitial : toutes se recalculent depuis l'état, aucune n'est mémorisée à côté.

nodes.label: Deux écrans, pas deux routes
nodes.rationale: L'écran de fin remplace l'écran de jeu par dérivation (estFinie), pas par navigation : le module n'a pas de routeur et n'en a pas besoin, Scoreo tient la route.

nodes.label: Workflow: Deploy to GitHub Pages
nodes.rationale: Only apps/scoreo is built and deployed; modules are built by ci.yml. A dedicated step asserts every apps/scoreo/public/ asset made it into the artifact, so nothing added to public/ silently misses the deploy.

nodes.label: Deploy job: smoke-test of the deployed site
nodes.norm_label: deploy job: smoke-test of the deployed site

nodes.label: pnpm monorepo (host app + modules)
nodes.rationale: Scoreo is the only deployed app; per-game score counters become on-demand-loaded packages so a game's rules never weigh on the host bundle and can be developed and tested in isolation.

nodes.label: One PR per hygiene category
nodes.rationale: A combined PR mixing a dependency bump with a doc fix is harder to review and riskier to revert.

nodes.label: Dependabot 2-day cooldown vs pnpm minimumReleaseAge
nodes.rationale: pnpm refuses packages younger than 24h (ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION, seen on PR #176). Without a matching Dependabot cooldown, PRs open on packages too fresh and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails in CI until the package ages out; 2 days keeps a margin over pnpm's 24h window since the daily schedule drifts.

nodes.label: TypeScript >=7 pinned out of Dependabot
nodes.rationale: TypeScript 7.x crashes typescript-eslint whose peer dependency caps at <6.1.0 (PR #172); 6.x bumps keep flowing and the ignore is to be lifted once typescript-eslint supports TS 7.

nodes.label: Migration v1 → v2 (UUID ids + epoch dates)
nodes.norm_label: migration v1 → v2 (uuid ids + epoch dates)

nodes.label: Card-declared input counts
nodes.rationale: Each computable card declares the counts it needs, so no tile-by-tile board model is required. Cerisier C and Montagne C cross two landscapes (Cerisier value = Village tile count; Montagne bonus = adjacent Eau tiles), which the declared-counts shape still accommodates.

nodes.label: Winner and tie-break resolution
nodes.rationale: Highest total VP, then total Torī held, then Pinceau possession; an unresolved tie is shared and every tied player is handed rank 1 — carrying into Scoreo's history a rule Scoreo itself does not know.

nodes.label: Host (ModuleHost)
nodes.rationale: Scoreo, reachable only through the ModuleHost handed to the screen: getPlayers(), saveDraft(), saveMatch(). The single seam through which anything leaves the module.

nodes.label: Match (recorded playthrough)
nodes.rationale: Stored by Scoreo; the module's own grid travels with it as an opaque moduleData payload the host hands back untouched however old it is.

nodes.label: Module (scoring module)
nodes.rationale: A manifest plus a screen. It owns the game's rules and nothing else — no storage, no players, no history — so there is nothing left to abstract behind a port.

nodes.label: Hosted module public surface
nodes.rationale: src/module.ts is read eagerly by Scoreo's registry so it imports nothing but its type; the dynamic import inside load is what puts the screen in its own chunk. ScoreDetailScreen takes a save(results, objectifCards) callback rather than a use case, so it stays ignorant of where scores go.

nodes.label: Legacy tori_valley_* localStorage keys
nodes.rationale: tori_valley_players / _matches / _language are what the standalone app left behind on the origin it shared with Scoreo; read by nothing since #350. The module now writes no key at all — drafts live under Scoreo's scoreo_module_draft_tori-valley.

nodes.label: Artiste (player role)
nodes.rationale: 1-4 players, ~30 min, age 10+; turn order is clockwise and the Artiste who painted most recently starts.

nodes.label: Paysage Bambou
nodes.rationale: The only tile type that ever carries a Pinceau icon (7 across the whole tile set).

nodes.label: Carte Objectif
nodes.rationale: One card drawn at random per landscape type at setup, in A/B/C difficulty variants; the rulebook recommends the A set for a first game. The unused cards go back in the box, so the selection is fixed for the whole match.

nodes.label: Décompte des points (end-of-game scoring)
nodes.rationale: Four addends: +X PV for a Parchemin, +2 PV for the Pinceau, the Objectif points of each of the 5 landscapes, and the Torī collection points. This is exactly the shape the module's score entry captures.

nodes.label: Règle d'égalité (tie-break)
nodes.rationale: Ties go to the tied Artiste who painted the most Torī, then to whoever holds the Pinceau; an unresolved tie is shared.

nodes.label: Groupe de tuiles adjacentes
nodes.rationale: Two or more adjacent tiles of the same landscape form a group — the unit almost every Objectif card scores against.

nodes.label: Les Roues (tile market)
nodes.rationale: Two wheels hold the available tiles: a tile is takeable if it sits on an arrow slot or is adjacent to an empty space, so removals open up new choices. A wheel is refilled only once fully emptied.

nodes.label: Mode Solo
nodes.rationale: Scores against a simulated opponent board with a difficulty bonus — a compare-to-opponent flow, not the 1-4 players entering their own results the module models.
nodes.source_location: p.8 — Mise en place solo / Comparez votre score

nodes.label: Jeton Parchemin
nodes.rationale: The tile placed at the centre of the big wheel at setup fixes which landscape earns a Parchemin; the stack is 5/4/4/3 at 4 Artistes, 5/4/3 at 3, 5/3 at 2, highest remaining taken first, so the value depends on when it was claimed and how many players there are.

nodes.label: Jeton Pinceau
nodes.rationale: A single physical token: taken by placing a Bambou tile bearing the Pinceau icon, it lets its holder pick any tile around a wheel without restriction, then returns to the centre. Whoever holds it at game end scores +2 PV — hence at most one holder per match.

nodes.label: Plateau Tableau
nodes.rationale: Each Artiste's personal grid, carrying two special spot symbols: the Parchemin spot and the = rows that grant Sceaux.
nodes.source_location: p.6 — Les emplacements des plateaux Tableau

nodes.label: Règles de pose des tuiles
nodes.rationale: First tile must go on the bottom row; a tile on a higher row must be entirely supported by those below it (the board edge counts as support, so 2 tiles suffice in the left and right columns).
nodes.source_location: p.5 — Règles de pose des tuiles

nodes.label: Jeton Sceau
nodes.rationale: One-use special action per landscape (Eau swaps two tiles on a wheel; Bambou places with one support tile fewer; Montagne reserves a tile when a wheel refills; Village draws 3 from the bag and keeps 1; Cerisier swaps a tile at game end). Earned by placing 3 different landscapes on the = rows; max 2 per Artiste.
nodes.source_location: p.6-7 — Les jetons Sceau / Effets des Sceaux

nodes.label: Tuile Paysage
nodes.rationale: Five types (Cerisier, Montagne, Bambou, Eau, Village), drawn from a bag onto the wheels and placed on the player's Tableau.

nodes.label: Variante des tuiles Papier
nodes.rationale: Modifies the Tableau's shape with Papier tiles; it changes placement, not the scoring formula, which is why the module does not model it.

nodes.label: Torī Valley Package Guidance (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: Scoped to what is specific to the module; the workspace root CLAUDE.md governs language, backlog and commit conventions so the two copies cannot diverge.

nodes.label: Torī Valley Feature Overview
nodes.rationale: The module exists because Torī series scoring is a non-trivial combinatorial rule that is easy to get wrong by hand; it does not replace the physical game, only its end-of-game arithmetic.

nodes.label: Torī Valley Documentation Index
nodes.rationale: This directory documents the game only; repository-wide concerns (backlog, automation pipeline) live in the workspace doc/.

nodes.label: Torī Valley Module README
nodes.rationale: Absorbed from the standalone remhiit/toriValleyScoreBoard repo; the standalone shell (index.html, Vite config, service worker) was deleted because Scoreo is the only deployed app and the module now ships as an on-demand chunk.

nodes.label: Neighbour-dependent cards stay manual
nodes.rationale: Village variante A (+4 per neighbouring Tableau with strictly fewer Village tiles) and Eau variante C (+10 if your largest Water group beats every neighbour's) score against the neighbouring players' boards, which needs a seating order the app does not model. They show a short note and a plain total field.

nodes.label: Card scans kept local, never committed
nodes.norm_label: card scans kept local, never committed
nodes.rationale: Cropped photos of the 16 cards are the source of truth for the transcription, but the repository is public and the material is Origames copyright — so the directory is gitignored, same rule as the rulebook PDF, and a fresh clone must re-photograph the cards.

nodes.label: Guided Objectif entry
nodes.rationale: Score entry asks only for the one-to-three counts the selected card actually needs ('how many groups of exactly 2 Bamboo tiles?') and computes points from the card's own table — deliberately avoiding a tile-by-tile board model, since the player still reads the counts off their physical board. 13 of the 15 cards are computed this way.

nodes.label: Pre-guided matches open as hand-typed
nodes.rationale: Old results carry per-landscape totals with no counts behind them. Showing them as guided would put the stored points above a form reading all zeros, and the first keystroke would rescore from those zeros — so the override starts ticked and un-ticking it is a deliberate act.

nodes.label: Per-landscape manual override
nodes.rationale: Every card keeps a 'enter the total by hand' tickbox whose typed value wins — the escape hatch if a transcribed scoring table turns out to be wrong. Un-ticking recomputes from whatever counts were already entered.

nodes.label: Rules deliberately not modeled
nodes.rationale: Sceau effects only change what a player could place during the physical game, never the final tally; the Papier tile variant has no scoring effect; solo mode is a different flow entirely. None of the three earns a score input.

nodes.label: An untouched count reads as zero
nodes.norm_label: an untouched count reads as zero
nodes.rationale: A half-filled card scores what its form actually says rather than falling back to a total the screen never showed; an out-of-bounds count holds that landscape at 0 until corrected.

nodes.label: Zod .default() backward-compat rule
nodes.rationale: Adding a field to a persisted model must give it a zod .default() so data written by an older app version keeps loading; schemas parse on read and fail open (unparseable JSON → empty result) rather than throwing.

nodes.label: No storage, no port, no adapter
nodes.norm_label: no storage, no port, no adapter
nodes.rationale: The ports, adapters, use cases and DI container went with the standalone shell (#330, #350): a module owns no storage, so it has nothing to abstract. Everything persisted goes through ModuleHost, stored by Scoreo under its own keys.

nodes.rationale: Mécanique de relance (au moins un dé réservé, minimum deux dés relancés, têtes de mort maudites) non portée par le module : Scoreo compte le résultat final, pas la table.

nodes.label: Les trois couches (hôte / écran / domaine)
nodes.rationale: Le domaine ne connaît rien, l'écran ne connaît que le domaine et le contrat, l'hôte n'est joignable qu'à travers ModuleHost. Rien ne touche localStorage.

nodes.label: Module de comptage (pas une application)
nodes.rationale: Le paquet n'a ni build, ni déploiement, ni stockage : joueurs, historique, stats, export, thème et persistance restent à l'hôte. Ce que le module possède, c'est le jeu.

nodes.label: ScoringModuleScreenProps (host, playerIds, editing, onExit)
nodes.rationale: Le module ne stocke jamais un nom de joueur, seulement un id : les noms viennent de host.getPlayers(). Rouvrir une partie (editing) gagne toujours sur le brouillon courant.

nodes.label: Documentation 1000 Sabords
nodes.rationale: La doc du jeu vit dans le paquet du module ; ce qui concerne le dépôt entier (build, CI, déploiement, contrat hôte/module) reste dans doc/ à la racine.

nodes.label: L'état de tour vivant
nodes.rationale: C'est la raison d'être de saveDraft/loadDraft/clearDraft dans le contrat de module.

nodes.label: Reprise après fermeture
nodes.rationale: Le module sauvegarde en continu la partie ET le tour en cours (dés, onglet, multiplicateur, carte) : fermer l'onglet en plein comptage ne perd rien — c'est précisément ce que l'application autonome perdait avant la fusion.

nodes.label: index.ts n'exporte que le manifeste et le module
nodes.norm_label: index.ts n'exporte que le manifeste et le module
nodes.rationale: Le registre de Scoreo l'importe de façon eager : tout ce qu'index.ts ré-exporterait voyagerait dans le bundle principal de l'hôte. Le domaine se rejoint par chemin relatif.

nodes.label: Le bug d'origine (EtatTour.kt non persisté)
nodes.rationale: L'app Kotlin gardait quatre variables mutables au niveau module (dés, onglet, multiplicateur, carte) sans les persister : un rechargement en plein tour jetait silencieusement la main qu'un joueur venait de compter.

nodes.label: Identité visuelle scopée (.module-mille-sabords + préfixe ms-)
nodes.rationale: Les deux, pas l'un ou l'autre : le scoping protège l'hôte du module, le préfixe protège le module de l'hôte. Vérifié statiquement par scripts/check-module-styles.mjs. styles.css est chargé par l'écran, donc voyage dans son chunk : le module arrive stylé et ne coûte rien tant que personne ne l'ouvre.

nodes.label: Workflow: Queue PR for Review
nodes.rationale: Clears stale review-pass/needs-fix and re-posts needs-review on every opened/ready_for_review/synchronize, so a push after a verdict automatically re-queues R3 instead of leaving an outdated verdict standing.

nodes.label: Workflow: Requeue Lost Routine Events (hourly sweeper)
nodes.norm_label: workflow: requeue lost routine events (hourly sweeper)
nodes.rationale: Routine events can be dropped past the daily run cap, so an hourly sweep re-posts orphaned ready/needs-review/needs-fix labels, catches up issues left open by auto-merged PRs, and promotes the next queued issue to ready.

nodes.label: Workflow: Review Status Sync (claude/review commit status)
nodes.norm_label: workflow: review status sync (claude/review commit status)
nodes.rationale: No tool available to a Claude Code session can post a raw commit status, so the LLM verdict surfaces as a label and this deterministic Action translates review-pass/needs-fix into the claude/review status on the PR head SHA.

nodes.label: R1 — grooming routine (issue → spec)
nodes.rationale: Always interactive, never autonomous: the grooming gate is where a human confirms the spec before any code-writing routine can fire.

nodes.label: R2 — implementation routine (one run, one ticket)
nodes.norm_label: r2 — implementation routine (one run, one ticket)
nodes.rationale: One run handles exactly the issue from its triggering event and never searches for another: issue #149 showed a session whose trigger issue was stale picking a different `ready` issue and risking a duplicate PR.

nodes.label: R3 — PR review routine
nodes.rationale: Reviews only what CI structurally cannot judge (spec conformance, layering, backward-compat, doc freshness, debt); re-checking lint/test/build by eye would waste the review on machine-verified facts.

nodes.label: R6 — weekly observability report routine
nodes.rationale: Not yet autonomous: automation-plan §6 holds that an unproven skill stays interactive until rodée over several real weeks.

nodes.label: doc/technical/automation-plan.md — target automation architecture
nodes.rationale: Labels act as the event bus between deterministic GitHub Actions and LLM routines, so each phase can be put into autonomy independently and rolled back by label alone.

nodes.label: 3-attempt cap on autonomous fixes (attempt-1/2/3)
nodes.rationale: The same disagreement surviving two fix attempts means a human decision is needed, not a third guess; the old attempt-N is cleared up front so two attempt labels never coexist and silently defeat the cap, and pr-review clears attempt-* on review-pass so a stale counter never bleeds into a later unrelated needs-fix.

nodes.label: Claim the run (clear the queue label first)
nodes.norm_label: claim the run (clear the queue label first)
nodes.rationale: A routine's GitHub trigger fires on ANY pull_request event while its queue label is present, so posting any later label re-triggers the same routine on the same PR. Removing needs-review / needs-fix before writing any other label closes that self-retrigger door (seen on PR #111, where R4 chained attempt-1→attempt-3→needs-human in a minute from its own label writes).

nodes.label: Guard against a moved HEAD before labelling a verdict
nodes.norm_label: guard against a moved head before labelling a verdict
nodes.rationale: review-status-sync.yml stamps claude/review onto the head SHA at the moment the labeled event fires; a push landing mid-review would get a verdict stamped onto a commit the review never read. needs-review-label.yml's synchronize handler mostly closes the window but webhook ordering is not guaranteed, so the SHA comparison stays load-bearing.

nodes.label: Workflow: Auto-Merge Sync
nodes.rationale: `gh pr merge --auto` completes asynchronously under the GITHUB_TOKEN identity, and GitHub never spawns a workflow run for GITHUB_TOKEN-triggered events — so pull_request.closed never reaches close-linked-issues.yml for these merges (#208/#212). Waiting for the merge inside the same job and closing the linked issues there sidesteps the limit.

nodes.label: Pre-commit Checklist
nodes.rationale: Doc updates are treated as part of the change, not an afterthought: a diff adding a reducer/use case/model/port/adapter without a matching doc/ update is considered incomplete, which keeps doc/ from drifting away from code.

nodes.label: Hexagonal architecture layering (Ports & Adapters)
nodes.rationale: Reducers stay pure in ui/*, business logic sits framework-free in application/, repository interfaces live in domain/port/ with implementations in infrastructure/ — a reducer reaching a repository is treated as a design error, routed through a use case instead.

nodes.label: Backward-compatible serialized models (zod .default())
nodes.rationale: All state lives in the user's localStorage, so old payloads must still deserialize: every added field carries a zod .default(), and every removal/rename needs a documented migration.

nodes.label: Skill: project-conventions
nodes.rationale: Has no content of its own and delegates to CLAUDE.md and doc/, so conventions live in exactly one place instead of drifting across six skill files; on disagreement CLAUDE.md wins.

nodes.label: Module entry-point bundle trap
nodes.rationale: Scoreo's registry imports src/index.ts eagerly, so anything reachable from it lands in the host's main bundle — 1000 Sabords re-exported its domain there and ~8 kB of scoring rules rode into index.js (#345). A separate chunk changes nothing; only a grep on the built host bundle proves it.

nodes.label: Turn in progress through host.saveDraft/loadDraft
nodes.rationale: 1000 Sabords' Kotlin ancestor kept its dice in module-level vars and a reload threw away the hand a player had just counted out; the module also stores the event log rather than a mutable aggregate so the reducer's output never depends on who else holds a reference.

nodes.label: Module stylesheet leak trap (both directions)
nodes.rationale: Scoping under .module-<id> protects the host from the module but not the reverse: Scoreo's theme.css styles plain .card/.empty, so a module reusing those names inherits them. Torī Valley shipped broken player cards for 35 hours (#331 → #348) because no static check knew and the visual suite still photographed the module's standalone shell — hence class prefixes plus check-module-styles.mjs in CI.

nodes.label: tori-valley i18next namespace
nodes.rationale: registerTranslations() adds the module's dictionaries to whatever instance the host provides when the chunk loads, so the two sets of strings share one instance without colliding. Language choice stays Scoreo's; the module has no bootstrap of its own.

nodes.label: Strictly inward dependency direction
nodes.rationale: ui → domain, and domain imports from nothing else — including no i18n dependency: domain errors carry a plain string code that the ui layer translates.

nodes.label: Module stylesheet scoping and tv- prefix
nodes.norm_label: module stylesheet scoping and tv- prefix
nodes.rationale: Every rule is scoped under .module-tori-valley and every class prefixed tv-, because the two stylesheets name tokens alike with different values (--color-primary Torī red vs Catppuccin mauve, --space-5 24px vs 20px, --radius-lg 16px vs 14px) and element selectors would have restyled the whole app for the rest of the session — a stylesheet is not unloaded on navigation. The prefix guards the other direction: Scoreo's theme.css styles plain .card and .empty, and reusing the name shipped a real layout bug (#349). check-module-styles.mjs fails on either breach.

nodes.label: Visual regression suite lives in the host
nodes.norm_label: visual regression suite lives in the host
nodes.rationale: jsdom computes no layout, so behaviour tests can assert what the DOM says but never what the user sees. Playwright screenshots moved to the host with the shell because that is Scoreo's route, where players actually meet the module; the two suites never overlap.

nodes.label: Repository Ports Are Deliberately Not Shared
nodes.norm_label: repository ports are deliberately not shared

nodes.label: queued → ready one-at-a-time dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Posing several `ready` at once would fire that many R2 events simultaneously and, past the run cap (5/day on Pro), the excess events are simply lost. Promoting one queued issue at a time — only when nothing is ready/in-progress — bounds the event rate into R2 by construction. Labels are also posted one per call because GitHub fires one labeled webhook per label and a trigger filter matches the issue's current label state, not the label that named the event (issue #99).
